title: Prompt contrast experiments log
content:
Purpose:
- Quick scratchpad for comparing nearby prompt formulations (wording, instruction order, anchor examples) and logging visible failure modes.
- Aim: build a small prompt library of 'contrast pairs' to feed into automated stability tests later.

High-level idea (contrast testing):
- For a single task, construct 3 variants: instruction-first, example-first, and hybrid.
- Track a small set of heuristics per response: answer-accuracy (binary/approx), hallucination-flag (Y/N), format-adherence (Y/N), verbosity-score (0-3), response-divergence (pairwise BLEU/similarity).
- Quick manual runs on hosted API and on a 8-bit quantized private endpoint to see divergence due to quantization.

Quick TODOs: (prioritize)
- [ ] Build 10 contrast pairs for the 'customer-email-summarization' workflow.
- [ ] Add to eval harness: check for numeric fidelity (dates, monetary amounts).
- [ ] Write small script to compute 'divergence score' across model variants (hosted vs dedicated).
- [ ] Capture 30 failure examples to seed the few-shot bank.

Example task: short-email action item extraction
- Goal: from an incoming email, extract 0+ action items as bullet list with 'actor', 'action', 'due' fields.

Variant A (instruction-first):
"You are an assistant that extracts action items from a short email. Output only a JSON array of items with keys 'actor', 'action', 'due'. If a field is unknown, use null. Do not add commentary."

Variant B (example-first):
"Example:
Email: 'Can you check the Q3 metrics and update the deck by Friday? — Sam'
Output: [{actor: 'Sam', action: 'update deck with Q3 metrics', due: 'Friday'}]
Now do the same for the email below:
Email: 'FYI we'll need a legal review on the new contract, deadline Oct 12 — Priya'
"

Variant C (hybrid, constrained):
"You are a terse extractor. Follow this exact JSON schema: [ { 'actor': string | null, 'action': string | null, 'due': string | null } ]. If there are no actions, return an empty array. No extra keys, no commentary."

Notes from quick runs (2024-04-12):
- Hosted default model (open-rl-1): Variant A tends to produce extra commentary before JSON ~30% of runs (format-adherence fail).
- Dedicated quantized instance: got repeated actor names when emails had pronouns (e.g., 'Can we review it?'). Hypothesis: truncated context for pronoun resolution in batching.
- Example-first (B) reduces hallucination of dates but sometimes copies full sentence into 'action' instead of condensing.

Failure-mode catalog (informal):
1) Format bleed: assistant appends 'Note:' lines before/after JSON despite explicit 'only JSON' instruction. This often correlates with prompts that include examples with extra commentary.
2) Numeric-collapse: amounts/dates change format or drop tokens under heavy sampling temp>0.7.
3) Pronoun drift: When few-shot examples use 'Sam' but test email uses 'I'/'we', model sometimes maps 'I'->'Sam' if nearest example bias is strong.
4) Repetition-on-truncation: Long context + large kernel latency -> partial generation repeated at the end of tokens.
5) Failure to follow schema for empty result: returns null instead of [] or returns 'No actions' as free text.

Quick few-shot sets (3-shot) for action-extraction (try swapping orders):
Set 1 (order: actor->action->due in each example)
- Ex1: Email: 'Please review the PR and approve it by Tue — Alice' -> [{actor: 'Alice', action: 'review and approve PR', due: 'Tue'}]
- Ex2: Email: 'We need a security scan before release, target 2024-05-18 — EngOps' -> [{actor: 'EngOps', action: 'run security scan', due: '2024-05-18'}]
- Ex3: Email: 'Ping: can you draft the vendor note? end of month — Miguel' -> [{actor: 'Miguel', action: 'draft vendor note', due: 'end of month'}]

Set 2 (shuffle: due first)
- Ex1: 'Due Fri: finalize onboarding docs — People Team' -> [{actor: 'People Team', action: 'finalize onboarding docs', due: 'Fri'}]
- Ex2/3 similar

Observations: ordering in examples affects where the model focuses. When 'due' is first, model is better at normalizing dates but slightly worse at actor extraction for short senders.

Edge-case prompts to add to library (to test fail modes):
- Emails with nested bullets, embedded quoted replies, or inline signatures.
- Emails with no explicit actor (e.g., 'Can someone on infra...') -> expect actor: null or 'team: infra' heuristic.
- Ambiguous dates: 'next Monday' relative to created_at — test with frozen reference dates.

Small checklist for converting these to automated tests:
- Canonicalize input (strip signatures, normalize whitespace).
- Include a 'reference date' field in metadata for 'relative date' resolution.
- For every test, snapshot raw model output and normalized parse.
- Add label: 'format-violation' if parse fails to match schema.

Failure exemplars (copy/paste raw)
- Input: 'Can you take this on? Thanks — Sam'
  Model output: 'Sam said: Sure, I'll take this on.
[ {actor: 'Sam', action: 'take this on', due: null} ]'  -> format bleed + commentary.

- Input: 'Legal needs this signed by Oct 12'
  Model output on quantized instance: 'signed by Oct 21' -> numeric-collapse / date drift.

Meta-notes / heuristics to try next:
- Add a short 'assistant persona line' like 'Respond concisely and only in the requested schema' but keep under 12 tokens. Small persona lines sometimes increase format adherence.
- Try using explicit labels for examples: 'EXAMPLE_START' 'EXAMPLE_END' — separators can reduce bleed.
- Test adding a trailing 'END_OF_RESPONSE' token to the prompt to nudge model to stop.

Tracking idea: 'contrast-id' naming convention
- Use names like AC-<task>-<variant>-<seed> e.g., AC-ACTION-EXTRACT-A-001 so that test harness can reference easily. Keep a small CSV mapping contrast-id -> prompt text -> expected schema.

Notes to self: experimental, messy. Save top 50 raw failure outputs into /tmp/prompt-failures-archive/ and then move to Confluence if we have 10 re-occurring patterns.

References / links used while testing:
- Short harness: https://github.com/redwood/repro-prompts (local branch: contrast-testing)
- Related ticket: JIRA-ENG-1298 (action extraction flake on dedicated).
- Slack conv: #prompt-lab thread 'action-extract-probe' (search for 'contrast pair run 2024-04-11').

Quick decisions for next week:
- Prioritize building 10 contrast pairs for the top three user-facing tasks: action-extraction, summary-to-bullets, intent-classification.
- Convert top 20 failure cases into deterministic unit tests in the harness.
- Try one automated run comparing hosted/default vs dedicated-quantized and log divergence scores.
